"""Entra ID settings of the desktop app (all public, none of them a secret)."""

from typing import Final

from pydantic import BaseModel

POSTGRES_SCOPE: Final = "https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default"
"""Access tokens for Azure Database for PostgreSQL."""


class DesktopConfig(BaseModel):
    tenant_id: str = ""
    client_id: str = ""
    """App registration of the desktop app: public client, redirect
    `http://localhost`, delegated permission for Azure OSSRDBMS."""
    db_scope: str = POSTGRES_SCOPE
    db_role: str = ""
    """Postgres role to log in as. Empty: the user's own principal (UPN).
    Set it to the Entra group name when the group is the database principal."""
    sign_in_timeout: int = 300  # seconds the browser sign-in may take

    @property
    def configured(self) -> bool:
        values = (self.tenant_id, self.client_id)
        return all(v and not v.startswith("<") for v in values)

    @property
    def authority(self) -> str:
        return f"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{self.tenant_id}"
"""Microsoft Entra ID sign-in and per-user Postgres access for the desktop app.

The app is a public client: MSAL runs the authorization code flow with PKCE in
the system browser (loopback redirect), there is no client secret. The token
cache lives in the macOS Keychain, so the user stays signed in across starts.

Postgres sees every user with their own identity: each new connection gets a
fresh access token as password (`install_db_auth`). Connections opened before
sign-in fail with `NotSignedInError`, which the session checks treat as
"not logged in".
"""

import logging
import sys
import threading
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Final

import msal
from platformdirs import user_data_dir
from sqlalchemy import event
from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine

from app.desktop.config import DesktopConfig

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

TOKEN_LIFETIME_FALLBACK: Final = 3600.0
"""Seconds an access token lives when Entra does not say (it usually does)."""
REFRESH_MARGIN: Final = 300.0
"""Renew this many seconds before the token expires."""
EXPIRY_SLACK: Final = 60.0
"""Never hand out a token that expires within this many seconds."""
RETRY_SECONDS: Final = 60.0
RESTORE_INTERVAL: Final = 30.0
"""Seconds between attempts to restore the cached account for a connection."""
KEYCHAIN_SERVICE: Final = "alloq"
KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT: Final = "entra-token-cache"


class SignInError(Exception):
    """Sign-in failed; the message is shown to the user."""


class NotSignedInError(RuntimeError):
    """A database connection was attempted before the user signed in."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Account:
    email: str
    name: str
    db_user: str


def token_cache(directory: Path | None = None) -> msal.TokenCache:
    """Encrypted token cache: Keychain on macOS, the OS store elsewhere."""
    from msal_extensions import (  # noqa: PLC0415  (optional native backends)
        PersistedTokenCache,
        build_encrypted_persistence,
    )
    from msal_extensions.persistence import KeychainPersistence  # noqa: PLC0415

    folder = directory or Path(user_data_dir("alloq", appauthor=False))
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    location = str(folder / "entra_token_cache")
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        persistence = KeychainPersistence(location, KEYCHAIN_SERVICE, KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT)
    else:
        persistence = build_encrypted_persistence(location)
    return PersistedTokenCache(persistence)


def _account(result: dict[str, Any], config: DesktopConfig) -> Account:
    if "access_token" not in result:
        detail = result.get("error_description") or result.get("error") or ""
        logger.warning("Entra sign-in failed: %s", result.get("error"))
        message = "Die Anmeldung bei Microsoft ist fehlgeschlagen."
        raise SignInError(f"{message} {detail}".strip())
    claims = result.get("id_token_claims") or {}
    email = str(claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or "")
    if not email:
        raise SignInError("Das Microsoft-Konto liefert keine E-Mail-Adresse.")
    return Account(
        email=email,
        name=str(claims.get("name") or email),
        db_user=config.db_role or email,
    )


class EntraSignIn:
    """MSAL public client with the signed-in account of this app process.

    The access token is kept with its expiry and renewed by a background
    thread shortly before it runs out, so new database connections (opened on
    the event loop) rarely have to wait for Entra.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        config: DesktopConfig,
        cache: msal.TokenCache | None = None,
        client_factory: Callable[..., Any] = msal.PublicClientApplication,
        timer_factory: Callable[..., Any] = threading.Timer,
        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
    ) -> None:
        self._config = config
        self._cache = cache
        self._client_factory = client_factory
        self._timer_factory = timer_factory
        self._clock = clock
        self._client: Any = None
        self._account: Account | None = None
        self._token: str | None = None
        self._expires_at = 0.0
        self._timer: Any = None
        self._last_restore = float("-inf")
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    @property
    def account(self) -> Account | None:
        return self._account

    def _app(self) -> Any:
        if not self._config.configured:
            raise SignInError(
                "Die Desktop-App ist nicht eingerichtet: Mandant und Client-ID "
                "fehlen in configuration/config.desktop.yaml."
            )
        if self._client is None:
            self._client = self._client_factory(
                self._config.client_id,
                authority=self._config.authority,
                token_cache=self._cache if self._cache is not None else token_cache(),
            )
        return self._client

    def _silent_result(self) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
        app = self._app()
        for cached in app.get_accounts():
            result = app.acquire_token_silent([self._config.db_scope], account=cached)
            if result and "access_token" in result:
                return result
        return None

    def _remember(self, result: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Keep the token and schedule its renewal (caller holds the lock)."""
        lifetime = float(result.get("expires_in") or TOKEN_LIFETIME_FALLBACK)
        self._token = REDACTED
        self._expires_at = self._clock() + lifetime
        self._schedule_refresh(max(lifetime - REFRESH_MARGIN, RETRY_SECONDS))

    def _schedule_refresh(self, delay: float) -> None:
        if self._timer is not None:
            self._timer.cancel()
        self._timer = self._timer_factory(delay, self._refresh_in_background)
        self._timer.daemon = True
        self._timer.start()

    def _refresh_in_background(self) -> None:
        """Renew the token off the event loop; retry soon on a failure."""
        with self._lock:
            if self._account is None:
                return
            try:
                result = self._silent_result()
            except Exception:
                logger.exception("Background token refresh failed")
                result = None
            if result is None:
                self._schedule_refresh(RETRY_SECONDS)
                return
            self._remember(result)

    def sign_in_silently(self) -> Account | None:
        """Use the cached account, without opening a browser."""
        with self._lock:
            result = self._silent_result()
            if result is None:
                return None
            self._account = _account(result, self._config)
            self._remember(result)
            return self._account

    def restore(self) -> Account | None:
        """The signed-in account, else the one cached in the Keychain.

        Lets a returning user keep working after an app restart without the
        sign-in page. Tries at most every `RESTORE_INTERVAL` seconds and never
        opens a browser.
        """
        if self._account is not None:
            return self._account
        now = self._clock()
        if now - self._last_restore < RESTORE_INTERVAL:
            return None
        self._last_restore = now
        try:
            return self.sign_in_silently()
        except SignInError:
            return None

    def sign_in_interactively(self) -> Account:
        """Browser sign-in with PKCE; blocks until done or timed out."""
        result = self._app().acquire_token_interactive(
            scopes=[self._config.db_scope],
            prompt="select_account",
            timeout=self._config.sign_in_timeout,
        )
        with self._lock:
            self._account = _account(result, self._config)
            self._remember(result)
            return self._account

    def access_token(self) -> str:
        """A valid Postgres access token.

        A failed refresh keeps the account: the connection attempt fails, the
        next one (or the background refresh) tries again.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if self._account is None:
                raise NotSignedInError("Not signed in")
            if self._token and self._clock() < self._expires_at - EXPIRY_SLACK:
                return self._token
            result = self._silent_result()
            if result is None:
                raise NotSignedInError("Token refresh failed")
            self._remember(result)
            return str(self._token)

    def sign_out(self) -> None:
        """Forget the account here and in the token cache."""
        with self._lock:
            self._account = None
            self._token = None
            if self._timer is not None:
                self._timer.cancel()
                self._timer = None
            if self._client is not None:
                for cached in self._client.get_accounts():
                    self._client.remove_account(cached)


def connect_params(sign_in: EntraSignIn, cparams: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Fill user and password of a new Postgres connection."""
    account = sign_in.restore()
    if account is None:
        raise NotSignedInError("Not signed in")
    cparams["user"] = account.db_user
    cparams["password"] = sign_in.access_token()


_installed: list[EntraSignIn] = []


def install_db_auth(sign_in: EntraSignIn) -> None:
    """Authenticate every new database connection with the user's token."""
    if _installed:
        _installed[0] = sign_in
        return
    _installed.append(sign_in)

    @event.listens_for(Engine, "do_connect")
    def _token_password(
        _dialect: Any, _record: Any, _cargs: Any, cparams: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        connect_params(_installed[0], cparams)

# alloq als Desktop-App

Die Desktop-App ist eine Tauri-App mit eingebettetem Python-Backend
(reflex-desktop). Sie nutzt die zentrale Postgres-Datenbank und enthält keine
Geheimnisse: Jede Person meldet sich mit Microsoft Entra ID an und verbindet
sich mit ihrem eigenen Zugriffstoken mit Postgres.

## Ablauf der Anmeldung

1. „Mit Microsoft anmelden“ nutzt zuerst das gespeicherte Konto aus dem
   macOS-Schlüsselbund (Eintrag `alloq` / `entra-token-cache`). Gibt es keins,
   öffnet MSAL die Anmeldung im Standardbrowser (Authorization Code Flow mit
   PKCE, Rückleitung auf `http://localhost`).
2. Jede neue Datenbankverbindung bekommt Benutzer und Token der angemeldeten
   Person (`app/desktop/entra.py`). Vor der Anmeldung gibt es keine
   Verbindung.
3. Die App prüft die Schema-Version (`alembic_version`) gegen
   `app/desktop/schema.py`. Passt sie nicht, bricht die Anmeldung mit einem
   Hinweis ab. Migrationen laufen nur auf dem Server.
4. Die App sucht den alloq-Benutzer mit derselben E-Mail-Adresse (Groß- und
   Kleinschreibung egal) und öffnet die normale appkit-Sitzung. Neue Benutzer
   legt die Desktop-App nicht an.

Nach einem Neustart stellt die App das Microsoft-Konto aus dem Schlüsselbund
still wieder her, sobald sie die Datenbank braucht. Ist die alloq-Sitzung noch
gültig, geht es ohne Anmeldeseite weiter. Das Zugriffstoken erneuert ein
Hintergrund-Thread kurz vor Ablauf.

„Abmelden“ beendet die Sitzung, vergisst das Microsoft-Konto auf diesem Mac und
schließt alle Datenbankverbindungen.

## Einrichtung in Azure (einmalig)

### App-Registrierung

Die Werte stehen in `configuration/config.desktop.yaml` unter `app.desktop`.
Die Datei verweist mit `secret:` auf die Einträge der Web-App; beim Build
löst `scripts/desktop.py` sie auf und schreibt die Werte in die App.
Erlaubt ist das nur für öffentliche Kennungen (`tenant_id`, `client_id`,
`host`, `name`); jedes andere `secret:` bricht den Build ab.

Die Registrierung braucht:

- Plattform „Mobile und Desktopanwendungen“ mit der Umleitungs-URI
  `http://localhost`.
- „Öffentliche Clientflows zulassen“: Ja. Die Desktop-App sendet kein
  Client-Secret.
- Delegierte API-Berechtigung „Azure OSSRDBMS Database“ →
  `user_impersonation`, mit Administratorzustimmung.

Wird dieselbe Registrierung wie für die Web-App genutzt, gelten diese
Einstellungen zusätzlich zur Web-Plattform.

### Postgres (Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Flexible Server)

1. Microsoft-Entra-Authentifizierung aktivieren und einen Entra-Admin setzen.
2. Als Entra-Admin die Prinzipale anlegen, entweder je Person
   (`SELECT * FROM pgaadauth_create_principal('ada@firma.de', false, false);`)
   oder einmal für eine Entra-Gruppe, z. B. `alloq-desktop`.
   Bei einer Gruppe in `config.desktop.yaml` `db_role: alloq-desktop` setzen;
   die Personen melden sich dann mit dem Gruppennamen an.
3. Rechte vergeben, z. B. über eine Rolle `alloq_app`:

   ```sql
   GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO alloq_app;
   GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO alloq_app;
   GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO alloq_app;
   GRANT alloq_app TO "ada@firma.de";  -- oder TO "alloq-desktop"
   ```

4. Netzwerk: Der Server muss von den Rechnern aus erreichbar sein (VPN oder
   Firewall-Regel). TLS ist Pflicht (`ssl_mode: require`).

Wichtig: Wer Datenbankrechte hat, kann mit seinem Token auch direkt auf die
Datenbank zugreifen, an den Admin-Prüfungen der App vorbei. Die Rolle deshalb
nur Personen geben, die in alloq Administratorrechte haben.

## Bauen und starten

```bash
task desktop:doctor
```

```bash
task desktop:run
```

```bash
task desktop:build
```

`task desktop:dev` startet die App mit Hot Reload gegen den Entwicklungsserver,
mit vorgetäuschter Anmeldung als `admin@aila-solutions.com` gegen die lokale
Datenbank (siehe unten). Ein anderer Benutzer:
`ALLOQ_FAKE_ENTRA_EMAIL=<email> task desktop:dev`.
Das Desktop-Profil gilt, sobald `ALLOQ_DESKTOP=1` gesetzt ist oder die App im
Bundle läuft (`app/desktop/profile.py`).

### Testen ohne Microsoft-Anmeldung

Für Entwicklung und Tests lässt sich die Anmeldung vortäuschen:

```bash
ALLOQ_DESKTOP=1 ALLOQ_FAKE_ENTRA_EMAIL=admin@aila-solutions.com uv run reflex run
```

„Mit Microsoft anmelden“ meldet dann ohne Browser als dieser alloq-Benutzer
an, und die Datenbank nutzt die lokalen Zugangsdaten (Profil
`desktop_fake`, Frontend auf Port 18443). Eine abweichende Schema-Version ist
dabei nur eine Warnung. Im App-Bundle wird die Variable ignoriert, und der
Build packt das Profil `desktop_fake` nie ein. Läuft daneben der normale
Entwicklungsserver, mit `REFLEX_WEB_WORKDIR=<anderer Ordner>` einen eigenen
`.web`-Ordner nutzen.

Nach einer neuen Migration muss `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py`
ergänzt werden; ein Test erinnert daran.

# AGENTS.md

---

## 1) Golden Rules

**NEVER** guess — **ALWAYS** read the doc first (use Context7 or a skill)!

1. **Think → Memory → Tools → Code → Memory.** Use code-reasoning; search Memory and claude-context first; minimal diff; write learnings back.
2. **Tests are truth.** Failures → fix code first. Change tests only if clearly wrong spec.
3. **Minimal diff.** Add tests before code. Keep simple.
4. **Consistency > cleverness.** Follow SOPs and stack idioms.
5. **Memory multiplies.** Persist decisions, patterns, error signatures, proven fixes.
6. **Files ≤ 1000 lines.** Exceed → refactor (see §5).
7. No extensive docs/summaries/comments unless requested.
8. No `cat` to create files; use tools.
9. Log default: `logger.debug`. Important events: `logger.info`. Issues only: `logger.warning/error`. **No `print`.**

> Prefer *local* changes over cross-module refactors.

---

## 2) Task Bootstrap Pattern

```markdown
<!-- plan:start
goal: <one line clear goal>
constraints:
- Python 3.14; FastAPI; Pydantic 2.13; pydantic-settings;
- logging: no f-strings in logger calls
- files ≤ 1000 lines; apply design patterns where appropriate
- minimal diff; add/adjust tests first
- hexagonal architecture: domain/application/ports/adapters/interfaces
definition_of_done:
- tests pass; coverage ≥ 80%; lint/type checks clean; memory updated
steps:
1) Search Memory for "<keywords>"
2) Draft/adjust failing test to capture expected behavior
3) Implement minimal code change
4) Run task test; iterate until green
5) Update Memory: decisions, patterns, error→fix
plan:end -->
```

---

## 3) Tooling Decision Matrix

| Situation | Primary | Secondary | Store to Memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API/pattern uncertainty | **Context7** | — | Canonical snippet + link; edge cases |
| Ecosystem bug/issue | **DuckDuckGo** | Context7 | Minimal repro; versions; workaround |
| Repeated test failure | **Memory (search)** | Context7 | Error signature → fix; root cause |
| New feature scaffold | **Context7** | — | How‑to snippet; checklist |
| House style/tooling | **This file** | Context7 | Checklist results |

Prefer official docs; widen via web search for cross-version issues.

---

## 4) SOP — Development Workflow

**Task Runner:** `task` (via `Taskfile.dist.yml`), not `make`.

### Prepare

1. Memory first — search prior solutions.
2. Reasoning plan — Task Bootstrap Pattern.
3. `task test` — snapshot current failures.

### Triage Failures

- Read first failing assertion; map to spec.
- Tests match spec → fix code. Diverge → document; adjust spec/tests (after approval).
- Add/adjust unit tests to codify expected behavior.

### Implement (Minimal Diff)

- Tests-first for new behavior. Approved stacks only. Apply design patterns (see §5).
- **No `print`.** Use `logging` module.

# Infrastructure

The Terraform code in `terraform/` describes the Azure resources. One Container
App runs Caddy and every Reflex app listed in `apps.yaml`. The code started as a
copy of the KnowledgeAI Admin infrastructure and uses the same remote state, so
the existing resources are kept.

## What Terraform creates per app

`terraform/apps.tf` reads `../apps.yaml` (variable `apps_file`). From it
Terraform creates:

- for every app, one database on the shared PostgreSQL Flexible Server, named
  `database.name`,
- for every app, the Key Vault secrets `<keyvault_prefix>-db-host`, `-db-name`,
  `-db-user` and `-db-password` (all apps share the server admin login),
- one Key Vault secret for every name under `config_secrets` of every app; the
  names belong to the app with that `keyvault_prefix`,
- once for the platform, the common secrets in `common_secret_names`
  (`common-db-encryption-key`, `common-oauth-*`, `common-ai-foundry-*`).
  Apps do not list them. The
  list of every automatic secret is in
  [Secrets that exist already](../guide/apps-yaml#secrets-that-exist-already),
- for every entry `APP_VAR: secret-name` in an app's `secrets` map, one
  Container App secret that reads the Key Vault secret of the same name, and one
  container variable named after it (see [Secrets](../guide/apps-yaml#secrets)).

### Secret values

- **Managed**: Terraform knows the value and keeps it in sync. A secret is
  managed when its name, without the first segment (the app prefix or
  `common-`), is `oauth-azure-client-id`, `oauth-azure-client-secret`,
  `oauth-azure-tenant-id` (app registration), `ai-foundry-apikey`,
  `ai-foundry-endpoint`, `azure-api-key` or `azure-api-endpoint` (AI Foundry).
  So `common-oauth-azure-client-id` and
  `avui-oauth-azure-client-id` are both filled from the app registration. The
  list is `known_secret_suffixes` in `terraform/apps.tf`.
- **Seeded**: every other name. It is created with the value from the variable
  `seed_values` or with `default`, and Terraform ignores later changes. Set the
  real value in the portal or with `az keyvault secret set`. A new secret for a
  new app is therefore empty at first and the app waits for you to fill it.

Terraform does not use the per app `env` and `build_env` maps. The image build
and supervisord read them.

## Same infrastructure as the original repository

With only `knowledgeai-admin` in `apps.yaml`, Terraform creates the resources of
the original KnowledgeAI-Admin repository: the same resource groups, network,
registry, log workspace, Container Apps environment, PostgreSQL server with the
one database `knowledgeai_admin`, identity, AI Foundry, app registration,
role assignments and the same Key Vault secrets with the same values. The email
service (Azure Communication Services) and its `avui-acs-*` secrets are gone.
The test `admin_only_matches_original_repository` checks the database
and the secret names and values. It uses `tests/fixtures/apps_admin_only.yaml`,
which lists the original `avui-*` names and sets `common_secret_names = []`.
The platform adds the `common-*` secrets on top of the original ones.

The app registration also gets the OAuth callback of every app in `apps.yaml`.
The Container App itself differs on purpose, because it runs the platform image:

#!/bin/sh
# Give an Entra ID principal (a group or a user) read and write access to the
# database of one app, e.g. the alloq desktop users. Run it once per principal
# after `terraform apply` with pg_entra_admin set; running it again is safe.
#
# Usage: postgres_entra_access.sh <keyvault> <keyvault-prefix> <entra-admin> <principal>
#
#   keyvault         Key Vault name (terraform output keyvault_name)
#   keyvault-prefix  keyvault_prefix of the app in apps.yaml, e.g. alloq
#   entra-admin      pg_entra_admin.principal_name; you must be that user or a
#                    member of that group
#   principal        Entra group display name or user UPN, e.g. alloq-desktop
#
# Step 1 logs in as the Entra admin with your `az login` token and creates the
# principal. Step 2 logs in as the server admin from <prefix>-db-* in Key Vault:
# that login owns the app's tables, so only it can grant on them. The principal
# gets the role <database>_app, which also covers tables of later migrations.
set -eu

if [ $# -ne 4 ]; then
  sed -n '6,13p' "$0" >&2
  exit 2
fi

vault=$1
prefix=$2
entra_admin=$3
principal=$4

secret() {
  az keyvault secret show --vault-name "$vault" --name "${prefix}-db-$1" --query value -o tsv
}

host=$(secret host)
database=$(secret name)
owner=$(secret user)
role="${database}_app"

echo "Creating the Entra ID principal ${principal} on ${host}"
PGPASSWORD=REDACTED account get-access-token --resource-type oss-rdbms --query accessToken -o tsv) \
  psql "host=${host} dbname=postgres user=${entra_admin} sslmode=require" \
  -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v principal="$principal" <<'SQL'
SELECT NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = :'principal') AS missing \gset
\if :missing
SELECT * FROM pgaadauth_create_principal(:'principal', false, false);
\endif
SQL

echo "Granting ${role} on database ${database} to ${principal}"
PGPASSWORD=REDACTED password) \
  psql "host=${host} dbname=${database} user=${owner} sslmode=require" \
  -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v principal="$principal" -v role="$role" -v database="$database" <<'SQL'
SELECT NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = :'role') AS missing \gset
\if :missing
CREATE ROLE :"role" NOLOGIN;
\endif
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE :"database" TO :"role";
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO :"role";
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO :"role";
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO :"role";
-- Tables and sequences that later migrations create as this login
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO :"role";
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO :"role";
GRANT :"role" TO :"principal";
SQL

echo "Done. Desktop users log in as ${principal} with their own token."

## OAuth callbacks

Admin and Alloq share the OAuth registrations, because both read the
`common-oauth-*` secrets. Each registration therefore needs the callback of both
apps:

- **Entra ID app registration**:

- **GitHub OAuth app** (`common-oauth-github-*`):
  `https://<fqdn>/knai/oauth/github/callback` and
  `https://<fqdn>/alloq/oauth/github/callback`. A classic GitHub OAuth app has

## Entra ID login for PostgreSQL

The alloq desktop app has no database password. Every person signs in with
Microsoft Entra ID, and the app sends their access token as the Postgres
password. This is off by default. It needs three things in Azure: the server
accepts Entra ID tokens, the app registration may ask for a token for Postgres,
and Postgres knows the principal and its rights.

### Terraform

Set `pg_entra_admin` and, for computers outside Azure, `pg_client_ip_ranges`:

```hcl
pg_entra_admin = {
  object_id      = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx" # Entra group of the database admins
  principal_name = "knai-db-admins"
  principal_type = "Group"                                # or User, ServicePrincipal
}

pg_client_ip_ranges = {
  office = { start_ip_address = "203.0.113.10", end_ip_address = "203.0.113.10" }
}
```

With `pg_entra_admin` set, Terraform:

- turns on Entra ID login on the server. Password login stays on, because the
  apps and their migrations log in with the admin user from `<prefix>-db-*`,
- makes `pg_entra_admin` the Entra admin of the server,
- adds a firewall rule for every entry in `pg_client_ip_ranges`,
- adds to the app registration the public client redirect `http://localhost`
  and the delegated permission "Azure OSSRDBMS Database" `user_impersonation`,
  and grants admin consent for the whole tenant.

With `create_app_registration = false`, Terraform does not manage the
registration. It adds the permission with `azuread_application_api_access`
and sets the public client redirects with `azuread_application_redirect_uris`.
That resource owns all public client redirects of the registration, so other
public client redirects of it are removed. Check in the portal that
"Allow public client flows" is on.

Before the first apply, check two things:

- The tenant has the service principal of "Azure OSSRDBMS Database"
  (`123cd850-d9df-40bd-94d5-c9f07b7fa203`). If the plan cannot find it, create it
  once with `az ad sp create --id 123cd850-d9df-40bd-94d5-c9f07b7fa203`.
- The account that runs Terraform may grant admin consent. If someone already
  granted consent in the portal, import that grant instead of creating a second
  one: `terraform import 'module.app_registration.azuread_service_principal_delegated_permission_grant.ossrdbms[0]' <grant id>`.

### Postgres

Postgres roles are not Azure resources, so Terraform does not create them. After
the apply, run once per principal:

```bash
az login
scripts/postgres_entra_access.sh <keyvault_name> alloq knai-db-admins alloq-desktop
```

The arguments are the Key Vault, the `keyvault_prefix` of the app, the Entra
admin, and the principal (an Entra group name or a user UPN). You must be the
Entra admin or a member of its group, and you need `psql` and read access to
the Key Vault. The script:

1. logs in as the Entra admin with your token and creates the principal with
   `pgaadauth_create_principal`,
2. logs in as the server admin from `<prefix>-db-*`, which owns the app's
   tables, and grants the role `<database>_app` to the principal. The role may
   read and change all tables, also the ones of later migrations, but may not
   change the schema.

Running the script again does no harm. With a group as principal, add people
to the Entra group; they log in as the group name. In the alloq desktop
configuration set `db_role` to the group name.

content.text:
The changes are committed on a new `feature/alloq2` branch in knowledgeai-container (commit `da50887`). The branch starts from the current `origin/main` and is not pushed yet. The Terraform tests (13, including 4 new ones), `terraform validate`, `task check` and pytest all pass.

The feature is off by default. As long as you don't set `pg_entra_admin`, the next plan shouldn't change anything in Azure.

**Terraform**
- **Turning it on:** two new optional settings in [variables.tf](../knowledgeai-container/terraform/variables.tf):
  - `pg_entra_admin` (Entra admin of the server, a group by default) switches the feature on.
  - `pg_client_ip_ranges` adds firewall rules for computers outside Azure.
- **Database module:** turns on Entra ID login on the server. Password login stays on, because the web apps and migrations still use the admin password. It also sets the Entra admin and adds the firewall rules.
- **App registration module:** adds the `http://localhost` redirect for the desktop app, the "Azure OSSRDBMS Database" `user_impersonation` permission, and admin consent for the whole tenant.
  - **Prod setup:** your example tfvars uses `create_app_registration = false`, so I also handled an existing registration. There the permission and redirect are added with separate resources instead of changing the registration itself.
  - **Watch out:** on an existing registration, Terraform then owns all "mobile and desktop" redirects. Any other redirects of that kind would be removed.

**Script for the database grants** ([scripts/postgres_entra_access.sh](../knowledgeai-container/scripts/postgres_entra_access.sh))
- On Azure the Entra admin is not a superuser, so it can create the principal but can't grant rights on tables owned by the password admin. The script therefore logs in twice:
  - as the Entra admin, with your `az login` token, to create the principal;
  - as the password admin from Key Vault, to create the role `<database>_app`. The role can read and write all tables, including ones from later migrations.
- I tested the grant part in a throwaway Postgres 16 container: running it twice is harmless, tables created later are covered, and the principal can't drop tables.
- The principal-creation part is not tested, because `pgaadauth_create_principal` only exists on Azure.

**Docs:** a new section in [infrastructure.md](../knowledgeai-container/docs/operations/infrastructure.md), a security note in [known-limits.md](../knowledgeai-container/docs/reference/known-limits.md), and an example block in `prod.auto.tfvars.example`.

**Before the first real apply:**
- The tenant needs the service principal of "Azure OSSRDBMS Database". If the plan can't find it, create it once with `az ad sp create --id 123cd850-d9df-40bd-94d5-c9f07b7fa203`.
- The account that runs Terraform must be allowed to grant admin consent.
- If consent was already granted in the portal, import that grant instead of creating a second one. The docs show the import command.

After that, set `db_role` in alloq's [config.desktop.yaml](configuration/config.desktop.yaml) to the group name (for example `alloq-desktop`). Also add the `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` step to [doc/desktop.md](doc/desktop.md), or point it to the script. Without it, tables from new migrations won't be readable by desktop users.

from appkit_commons.configuration.configuration import (
    ApplicationConfig,

from appkit_commons.registry import service_registry
from appkit_user.configuration import AuthenticationConfiguration

from app.desktop.config import DesktopConfig
from app.public_url import PUBLIC_BASE_URL_ENV, PublicUrl, apply_public_url

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class AppConfig(ApplicationConfig):
    authentication: AuthenticationConfiguration
    # Peer addresses allowed to set X-Forwarded-Proto. None trusts every peer,
    # so set it wherever the backend port is reachable without the proxy.
    trusted_proxies: set[str] | None = None
    # Entra ID sign-in of the desktop app (configuration/config.desktop.yaml).
    desktop: DesktopConfig | None = None


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def configure() -> Configuration[AppConfig]:
    logger.debug("--- Configuring application settings ---")
    config = service_registry().configure(
        AppConfig,
        env_file=".env",
    )
    public_url = PublicUrl.from_env()
    if public_url is not None:
        apply_public_url(public_url, config.reflex, config.app.authentication)
    elif config.app.environment == Environment.production:
        msg = f"{PUBLIC_BASE_URL_ENV} must be set in production"
        raise RuntimeError(msg)
    return config
"""Desktop profile: active before the configuration is loaded.

Called from `app/__init__.py`, right before `configure()`, so the import order
of `rxconfig` and `app` (it differs between `reflex run`, hot reload and the
embedded runtime) does not matter.
"""

import os
from typing import Final

DESKTOP_ENV: Final = "ALLOQ_DESKTOP"  # = alloq_commons.desktop.DESKTOP_ENV
DESKTOP_ROOT_ENV: Final = "REFLEX_DESKTOP_APP_ROOT"  # set by the Tauri host
DESKTOP_PROFILE: Final = "desktop"
FAKE_PROFILE: Final = "desktop_fake"
FAKE_ENV: Final = "ALLOQ_FAKE_ENTRA_EMAIL"


def is_desktop() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get(DESKTOP_ENV) == "1" or in_bundle()


def in_bundle() -> bool:
    """Running inside the built app (embedded backend)."""
    return DESKTOP_ROOT_ENV in os.environ


def activate_desktop_profile() -> None:
    """Add the desktop profile last, so it overrides every server value."""
    if not is_desktop():
        return
    os.environ[DESKTOP_ENV] = "1"
    profiles = [p for p in os.environ.get("PROFILES", "").split(",") if p.strip()]
    wanted = [DESKTOP_PROFILE]
    if os.environ.get(FAKE_ENV) and not in_bundle():
        wanted.append(FAKE_PROFILE)  # local DB credentials, development only
    missing = [p for p in wanted if p not in profiles]
    if missing:
        os.environ["PROFILES"] = ",".join([*profiles, *missing])


def prepare_embedded_backend() -> None:
    """The bundled app serves a prebuilt frontend; its payload has no assets/.

    Backend-only mode keeps `rx.asset` from checking files that only the
    frontend build needed.
    """
    if in_bundle():
        os.environ.setdefault("REFLEX_BACKEND_ONLY", "true")

# Manage Microsoft Entra Roles in Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server - Azure Database for PostgreSQL | Microsoft Learn

This article describes how to create Microsoft Entra ID-enabled database roles within an Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server.

To learn about how to create and manage Azure subscription users and their privileges, see the [Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC) article](/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles) or review [how to customize roles](/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/custom-roles).

Note

This guide assumes you already enabled Microsoft Entra authentication on your Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server.

## Create or delete Microsoft Entra administrators using Azure portal or Azure Resource Manager (ARM) API

1. Open the **Authentication** page for your Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in the Azure portal.
2. To add an administrator, select **Add Microsoft Entra Admin** and select a user, group, application, or a managed identity from the current Microsoft Entra tenant.
3. To remove an administrator, select the **Delete** icon for the administrator you want to remove.
4. Select **Save** and wait for the provisioning operation to complete.

Note

Support for Microsoft Entra Administrators management via Azure SDK, az cli, and Azure PowerShell is coming soon.

## Manage Microsoft Entra roles using SQL

After you create the first Microsoft Entra administrator from the Azure portal or API, you can use the administrator role to manage Microsoft Entra roles in your Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server.

For the best experience with Microsoft Entra integration in Azure Database for PostgreSQL, we recommend getting familiar with [Microsoft identity platform](/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/v2-overview).

### Principal types

Azure Database for PostgreSQL internally stores the mapping between PostgreSQL database roles and unique identifiers of Microsoft Entra objects. Each PostgreSQL database role can be mapped to one of the following Microsoft Entra object types:

- **User** - Including tenant local and guest users.
- **Service Principal** - Including [Applications and Managed identities](/en-us/azure/active-directory/develop/app-objects-and-service-principals).
- **Group** - When a PostgreSQL role is linked to a Microsoft Entra group, any user or service principal member of this group can connect to the Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server with the group role.

### List Microsoft Entra roles using SQL

```sql
select * from pg_catalog.pgaadauth_list_principals(isAdminValue boolean)
```

#### Arguments

##### `isAdminValue`

`boolean` - When `true`, returns admin users. When `false`, returns all Microsoft Entra users, including Microsoft Entra admins and nonadmins.

#### Return type

`TABLE(rolename name, principalType text, objectId text, tenantId text, isMfa integer, isAdmin integer)` - A table with the following schema:

- `rolename` - The name of the role in PostgreSQL.
- `principalType` - The type of principal in Microsoft Entra ID. It can be `user`, `group`, or `service`.
- `objectId` - The identifier of the object in Microsoft Entra ID for this principal.
- `tenantId` - The identifier of the tenant hosting this principal in Microsoft Entra ID.
- `isMfa` - Returns a value of `1` if the user/role has MFA enforced.
- `isAdmin` - Returns a value of `1` if the user/role is an administrator in PostgreSQL.

## Create a user or role with a Microsoft Entra principal name

```sql
select * from pg_catalog.pgaadauth_create_principal(roleName text, isAdmin boolean, isMfa boolean)
```

#### Arguments

##### `roleName`

`text` name of the role to create. This name **must match the name of the Microsoft Entra principal**.

- For **users**, use the User Principal Name from the profile. For guest users, include the full name in their home domain with the #EXT# tag.
- For **groups** and **service principals**, use the display name. The name must be unique in the tenant.

##### `isAdmin`

`boolean` when `true`, creates a PostgreSQL admin user (member of the `azure_pg_admin` role and with CREATEROLE and CREATEDB permissions). When `false`, creates a regular PostgreSQL user.

##### `isMfa`

`boolean` when `true`, enforces multifactor authentication for this PostgreSQL user.

Important

The `isMfa` flag tests the `mfa` claim in the Microsoft Entra ID token, but it doesn't impact the token acquisition flow. For example, if the tenant of the principal isn't configured for multifactor authentication, it prevents the use of the feature. And if the tenant requires multifactor authentication for all tokens, it makes this flag useless.

#### Return type

`text` single value that consists of a string "Created role for ***roleName***", where ***roleName*** is the argument you pass for the **roleName** parameter.

## Drop a role with a Microsoft Entra principal name

You can drop a role that corresponds to a Microsoft Entra ID principal in three ways:

- The Azure portal
- The Azure Resource Manager (ARM) API
- By executing the following SQL statement:

    ```sql
    DROP ROLE rolename;
    ```

Note

The Azure portal displays only admin roles. To drop a nonadmin role, use either the Azure Resource Manager (ARM) API or the SQL statement.

## Create a role by using the Microsoft Entra ID object identifier

```sql
select * from pg_catalog.pgaadauth_create_principal_with_oid(roleName text, objectId text, objectType text, isAdmin boolean, isMfa boolean)
```

#### Arguments

##### `roleName`

`text` name of the role to create.

##### `objectId`

`text` unique object identifier of the Microsoft Entra object.

- For **users**, **groups**, and **managed identities**, find the `objectId` by searching for the object name in [Microsoft Entra ID](https://ms.portal.azure.com/#blade/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/ActiveDirectoryMenuBlade) page in Azure portal. [See this guide as an example](/en-us/partner-center/find-ids-and-domain-names).
- For **groups** and **service principals**, use the display name. The name must be unique in the tenant.
- For **applications**, use the objectId of the corresponding **Service Principal**. In Azure portal, find the required objectId on [Enterprise Applications](https://ms.portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_IAM/ActiveDirectoryMenuBlade/%7E/EnterpriseApps) page.

##### `objectType`

`text` type of Microsoft Entra object to link to this role. It can be `user`, `group`, or `service`.

##### `isAdmin`

`boolean` when `true`, creates a PostgreSQL admin user (member of the `azure_pg_admin` role and with CREATEROLE and CREATEDB permissions). When `false`, creates a regular PostgreSQL user.

##### `isMfa`

`boolean` when `true`, enforces multifactor authentication for this PostgreSQL user.

Important

The `isMfa` flag tests the `mfa` claim in the Microsoft Entra ID token, but it doesn't impact the token acquisition flow. For example, if the tenant of the principal isn't configured for multifactor authentication, it prevents the use of the feature. And if the tenant requires multifactor authentication for all tokens, it makes this flag useless.

#### Return type

`text` single value that consists of a string "Created role for ***roleName***", where ***roleName*** is the argument you pass for the **roleName** parameter.

## Enable Microsoft Entra authentication for an existing PostgreSQL role using SQL

Azure Database for PostgreSQL uses security labels associated with database roles to store their corresponding Microsoft Entra ID mapping.

Use the following SQL to assign the required security label and map it to a Microsoft Entra object:

```sql
SECURITY LABEL for "pgaadauth" on role "<roleName>" is 'aadauth,oid=<objectId>,type=<objectType>,admin';
```

#### Arguments

##### `roleName`

`text` name of an existing PostgreSQL role to enable Microsoft Entra authentication.

##### `objectId`

`text` unique object identifier of the Microsoft Entra object.

##### `objectType`

`text` set to `user`, `group`, or `service` (for applications or managed identities connecting under their own service credentials).

##### `admin`

`text` set to present or absent. If present in the security label, users or roles can manage other Microsoft Entra ID roles.

The search confirms the function runs on the `postgres` database, but it didn't cover granting those roles access to other databases.

- **Where to run it:** A Microsoft Community Hub post says pgaadauth_create_principal must be run on the Postgres database. It's typically run while connected as the Entra administrator.
- **Signature:** The function takes a role name, an admin flag, and an MFA flag: pgaadauth_create_principal(roleName text, isAdmin boolean, isMfa boolean).
- **Naming:** The role name must match the Entra principal. For users, that's the user principal name, with the #EXT# tag for guest users. For groups and service principals, it's the display name.
- **Admin flag:** Setting it to true creates a role that is a member of the azure_pg_admin role and with CREATEROLE and CREATEDB permissions. Setting it to false creates a regular user.
- **Example:** Microsoft's group-login guide uses select * from pgaadauth_create_principal('Prod DB Readonly', false, false). to create a group role.
- **Dropping roles:** Microsoft's docs say that an Entra-created role must be dropped using a Microsoft Entra Admin. If you use a regular PostgreSQL admin to drop an Entra role then it will result in an error.

**Gap:** None of the results explain how to grant a created role connect or privileges on a different database (for example, `GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE ...`). For that, check Microsoft's Entra role documentation or run a follow-up search on granting database privileges to Entra roles in Azure Database for PostgreSQL.

# Writing Python Code

## Quick reference

- **Python 3.14** only; deps via **uv**; line length **88** chars (Ruff/Black).
- **No f-strings in logger calls** — use `log.info("x: %s", val)`.
- **Type annotations** on every function and method.
- **Files ≤ 1000 lines** — refactor via Extract Class, Mixins, Strategy, etc.
- **Coverage ≥ 80%** for non-Reflex classes and Reflex State classes.
- **Task runner:** `task format`, `task lint`, `task test` (not `make`).

## Code style

### Logging

```python
import logging

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

log.info("Loaded items: %d", count)          # ✅ parameterized
# log.info(f"Loaded items: {count}")         # ❌ f-string
```

Never use `print` or `printf`. Log levels: `debug` → internal state (default), `info` → milestones, `warning` → recoverable, `error` → serious.

### Type hints

```python
def process(data: dict[str, Any], count: int = 0) -> list[str]: ...

async def handler(value: str) -> AsyncGenerator[Any, Any]:
    yield
```

- Do not mix `Literal[...]` with `str` — pick one.
- Remove unused imports immediately (F401).
- Remove unused args or prefix with `_` (ARG001).

### Imports & formatting

- Ruff handles lint + format; run `task format` before committing.
- Break long calls/strings to fit 88 chars.

### Ruff rules to watch (project-specific)

| Code | Rule | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **UP031** | No `%`-formatting outside logger calls — use f-strings | Replace `"x %s" % val` with `f"x {val}"` |
| **I001** | Import order | Auto-fixed by `task format` |
| **PLC0415** | No local imports inside functions or test methods | Move to top of file |
| **B017** | `pytest.raises(Exception)` too broad | Use specific exception, e.g. `pytest.raises(ValidationError)` |

## File size rule

No Python file may exceed **1000 lines**. When approaching the limit, apply clean code refactoring strategies.

**Design patterns & refactoring strategies:** See skill [python-clean-code](../python-clean-code/SKILL.md).

## Testing

Coverage target: **≥ 80%** for services, repositories, models, utilities, and Reflex State classes. UI component rendering is best-effort.

```bash
task test                           # full suite with coverage
uv run pytest tests -k assistant    # targeted
uv run pytest tests -x              # stop on first failure
```

**Test patterns, fixtures, Reflex State testing:** See [references/testing.md](references/testing.md).

## Security & config

- No credentials in code/history; use `.env` locally, Key Vault in prod.
- Access Pydantic `SecretStr` via `.get_secret_value()`.
- Parameterized logs; avoid sensitive values.
- Use `appkit_commons.database.session_manager.get_session_manager().session()` for DB access outside Reflex handlers (not `rx.session()`).

## Database operations

```python
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

async def get_user(session: AsyncSession, user_id: int) -> User | None:
    result = await session.execute(
        select(User).where(User.id == user_id)
    )
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()
```

- Do NOT use `--autogenerate` for Alembic migrations; write them manually.
- BaseRepository methods must not commit; transaction boundaries are owned by the caller.

## Workflow

1. `task sync` to install/update deps.
2. **Read the docs first.** If something isn't working, use Context7 or DuckDuckGo to verify the correct API — never guess or change code blindly.
3. Write or adjust tests first (`tests/test_*.py`).
4. Implement minimal diff.
5. `task format && task lint && task test`.
5. Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `chore:`.

## Pre-commit checklist

- [ ] Tests pass (`task test`)
- [ ] Coverage ≥ 80%
- [ ] Lint/format clean (`task format && task lint`)
- [ ] No file exceeds 1000 lines
- [ ] No secrets in code
- [ ] Logging uses parameterized formatting
- [ ] All functions have type annotations

# Reflex Best Practices

This skill guides development in this Reflex.dev project. Read it before writing any new feature.

---

## 1. Project Architecture

Every feature lives in its own workspace package under `components/alloq-<name>/`. The main `app/` is the shell that assembles packages into a running application.

```
components/alloq-<feature>/
└── src/alloq_<feature>/
    ├── __init__.py          # public exports only
    ├── configuration.py     # Pydantic config schemas
    ├── backend/             # or backend.py — pure Python, no Reflex
    │   ├── models.py        # SQLModel table + UI models
    │   ├── repository.py    # async DB access
    │   └── services/        # business logic
    ├── state/               # or state.py — rx.State subclasses
    ├── components/          # or components.py — UI functions
    └── pages.py             # page factory functions

app/
├── app.py                   # assembles packages, creates rx.App
├── configuration.py         # root AppConfig + configure()
├── roles.py                 # Role definitions for RBAC
├── styles.py                # global style dicts + stylesheets
├── states/                  # app-level states (HomeState, etc.)
├── components/              # app-level reusable components
└── pages/                   # app-level pages
```

**Rule**: business logic belongs in `backend/`, reactive state in `state/`, UI in `components/`, routing in `pages.py`. Never mix concerns.

---

## 2. State Management

### Base class

All states inherit from `rx.State`. When you need the authenticated user, inherit from `UserSession` (from `appkit_user`):

```python
import reflex as rx
from appkit_user.authentication.states import UserSession

class MyFeatureState(rx.State):  # no auth needed
    ...

class MyFeatureState(UserSession):  # auth needed
    user = await self.authenticated_user
```

### State variable conventions

```python
class MyFeatureState(rx.State):
    # Data — typed, always with a default
    items: list[MyModel] = []
    selected_item: MyModel | None = None

    # Loading / UI flags
    is_loading: bool = False
    is_saving: bool = False

    # Filters / form fields
    search_query: str = ""
    selected_month: int = datetime.now(UTC).month

    # Private (not serialized to frontend) — prefix with _
    _initialized: bool = False

    # Browser-persisted — use rx.LocalStorage
    selected_tab: str = rx.LocalStorage("default", name="my-tab", sync=True)
```

### Computed vars

Use `@rx.var` for derived values. Avoid heavy computation — keep these O(n) at most.
Use `@rx.var(cache=True)` when the computation is more expensive or depends on a subset of state:

```python
@rx.var
def filtered_items(self) -> list[MyModel]:
    q = self.search_query.lower()
    return [i for i in self.items if q in i.name.lower()]

@rx.var
def total_count(self) -> int:
    return len(self.items)

@rx.var
def selected_year_str(self) -> str:
    # Bridge int → str for select components
    return str(self.selected_year)
```

Use async `@rx.var` only for DB queries that must stay reactive:

```python
@rx.var
async def chart_data(self) -> list[dict]:
    user = await self.authenticated_user
    async with rx.asession() as session:
        ...
```

### Event handlers

**→ See [`examples/state_example.py`](examples/state_example.py) for full annotated examples.**

```python
# Sync handler
@rx.event
def set_filter(self, value: str) -> None:
    self.search_query = value

# Async handler — yield after each mutation to push state to frontend
@rx.event
async def load_data(self) -> AsyncGenerator:
    self.is_loading = True
    yield
    try:
        self.items = await my_repo.get_all()
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to load")
        yield rx.toast.error("Laden fehlgeschlagen", position="top-right")
    finally:
        self.is_loading = False

# Chaining: iterate over another handler
async for _ in self.load_data():
    yield

# Background task — state mutations inside `async with self:`
@rx.event(background=True)
async def export_data(self) -> AsyncGenerator:
    async with self:
        self.is_exporting = True
    yield
    # ... heavy work ...
    async with self:
        self.is_exporting = False
    yield rx.toast.success("Fertig", position="top-right")

# Background task invocation — always yield the method reference
yield MyState.export_data
```

### Page on_load pattern

```python
@rx.event
async def on_load(self) -> AsyncGenerator:
    """Called via on_load=[MyState.on_load] in the page factory."""
    async for _ in self.load_data():
        yield
```

### Cache invalidation

```python
def _clear_caches(self) -> None:
    self.items.clear()
    self.expanded_rows.clear()
    self.detail_cache.clear()
```

---

## 3. UI Components — appkit_mantine

### Documentation rule

**Before using any `mn.*` or `rx.*` component not shown in [`examples/components_example.py`](examples/components_example.py), look up its API in the official documentation via the Context7 MCP server:**

```
# For appkit_mantine / Mantine components:
resolve-library-id("mantine")  → then get-library-docs(id, topic="<component name>")

# For Reflex-specific components and primitives:
resolve-library-id("reflex")   → then get-library-docs(id, topic="<component name>")
```

Additional real-world usage examples are available in the appkit repository:
**https://github.com/jenreh/appkit/tree/main/app/pages/examples**

| File | Components covered |
|---|---|
| `button_examples.py` | `mn.button`, `mn.action_icon`, `mn.action_icon.group` |
| `input_examples.py` | `mn.text_input`, `mn.textarea`, `mn.number_input`, `mn.tags_input`, `mn.password_input`, `mn.json_input`, `mn.slider`, `mn.range_slider`, `mn.switch` |
| `date_examples.py` | `mn.date_input`, `mn.date_picker_input`, `mn.date_time_picker`, `mn.month_picker_input`, `mn.time_input`, `mn.calendar` |
| `modal_examples.py` | `mn.modal`, `mn.modal.root`, `mn.modal.stack` |
| `overlay_examples.py` | `mn.tooltip`, `mn.hover_card` |
| `table_examples.py` | `mn.table`, `mn.table.thead/tbody/tr/th/td`, `sticky_header`, `with_table_border` |
| `charts_examples.py` | `mn.bar_chart`, `mn.line_chart`, `mn.area_chart` |
| `data_display_examples.py` | `mn.badge`, `mn.avatar`, `mn.card`, `mn.progress` |
| `navigation_examples.py` | `mn.tabs`, `mn.nav_link`, `mn.breadcrumbs` |
| `feedback_examples.py` | `mn.alert`, `mn.notification`, `mn.loader` |
| `combobox_examples.py` | `mn.select`, `mn.multi_select`, `mn.combobox` |

Always check the docs for:
- Correct prop names (e.g. `left_section` not `leftSection`, `with_border` not `withBorder`)
- Event handler signatures (`on_change`, `on_blur`, `on_visibility_change`)
- Controlled (`value=` + `on_change=`) vs uncontrolled (`default_value=` + `on_blur=`) usage

**→ For all component API, usage patterns, and visual guidelines, use the `appkit-mantine-reference` skill.**

---

## 4. Component Functions

**→ See [`examples/components_example.py`](examples/components_example.py) for full annotated examples.**

### Always functions, never classes

Component functions accept state vars as arguments for reactivity:

```python
def my_card(title: str, value: rx.Var | str) -> rx.Component:
    return mn.card(mn.heading(value, size="6", fw="bold"), ...)

# Correct — reactive binding
my_card(title="Users", value=MyState.user_count)
# Wrong — static, won't update
my_card(title="Users", value=42)
```

### Composition hierarchy

Build small → compose big. Prefix private helpers with `_`:

```python
def _filter_bar() -> rx.Component: ...
def _data_table() -> rx.Component: ...
def _empty_state() -> rx.Component: ...

def my_page_content() -> rx.Component:
    return mn.stack(
        _filter_bar(),
        rx.cond(MyState.is_loading, mn.loader(),
            rx.cond(MyState.items, _data_table(), _empty_state())),
        gap="md", w="100%",
    )
```

Use `rx.cond` and `rx.foreach` for conditionals and iteration — never bare Python `if` inside component functions.

---

## 5. Page Factory Pattern

**→ See [`examples/pages_example.py`](examples/pages_example.py) for the full annotated example including multi-page factories and registration.**

Every feature package exports a factory function (not a bare page):

```python
# pages.py
from appkit_user.authentication.templates import authenticated

def create_my_feature_page(navbar: rx.Component, route: str = "/my-feature", title: str = "My Feature") -> Callable:
    @authenticated(route=route, title=title, navbar=navbar, on_load=MyFeatureState.on_load, admin_only=True)
    def my_feature_page() -> rx.Component:
        return rx.flex(header(title), my_page_content(), direction="column", gap="4", w="100%", p="2rem")
    return my_feature_page

# Register in app/app.py:
create_my_feature_page(app_navbar())
```

---

## 6. Service Registry & Dependency Injection

Use `service_registry()` (from `appkit_commons`) as the single IoC container.

### Configuration

```python
# configuration.py
from appkit_commons.registry import service_registry

class MyFeatureConfig(BaseConfig):
    api_url: str | None = None
    api_key: SecretStr | None = None
```

Register in `configure()` in `app/configuration.py` by adding to `AppConfig`:

```python
class AppConfig(ApplicationConfig):
    my_feature: MyFeatureConfig | None = None
```

### Services

```python
class MyService:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._config = service_registry().get(MyFeatureConfig)
```

Register in `app/app.py` `_initialize_services()` in dependency order.

### Accessing in state

```python
def _do_work(self) -> None:
    config = service_registry().get(MyFeatureConfig)
    svc = service_registry().get(MyService)
```

---

## 7. Repository Pattern

`BaseRepository` (from `appkit_commons`) already provides full CRUD:
`create()`, `update()`, `save()`, `find_by_id()`, `find_all()`, `delete_by_id()`, `delete()`, `exists_by_id()`, `count()`

Only add custom methods for queries not covered by the base class (e.g., `find_by_email`, `find_all_paginated`):

```python
# backend/repository.py

from appkit_commons.repositories.base import BaseRepository
from appkit_commons.database.session import get_asyncdb_session
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

class MyModelRepository(BaseRepository[MyModelEntity]):

    async def find_by_name(
        self, session: AsyncSession, name: str
    ) -> MyModelEntity | None:
        result = await session.execute(
            select(MyModelEntity).where(MyModelEntity.name == name)
        )
        return result.scalar_one_or_none()


my_model_repo = MyModelRepository(MyModelEntity)
```

Always use `get_asyncdb_session()` — not `rx.asession()` — as the session factory:

```python
# In state event handlers
async with get_asyncdb_session() as session:
    items = await my_model_repo.find_all(session)
    entity = await my_model_repo.find_by_id(session, item_id)
    await my_model_repo.create(session, new_entity)
    await my_model_repo.update(session, entity)
    await my_model_repo.delete_by_id(session, item_id)
```

Never use `rx.asession()` — it does not work in background processors or callbacks outside the Reflex request lifecycle.

---

## 8. Database Models

### SQLAlchemy Entity (DB table)

Inherit from both `Entity` and `Base` from `appkit_commons.database.entities`. `Entity` provides `id`, `created`, and `updated` automatically. Add `to_dict()` for conversion to Pydantic/display models:

```python
# backend/entities.py
from appkit_commons.database.entities import Base, Entity
from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

class MyEntity(Entity, Base):
    __tablename__ = "my_feature_items"

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(default=True)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "name": self.name,
            "is_active": self.is_active,
        }
```

### Pydantic display model (UI-layer DTO)

Use `rx.Base` for models stored in Reflex state — never store SQLAlchemy `table=True` models directly:

```python
# backend/models.py
import reflex as rx

class MyModel(rx.Base):
    """UI-only DTO — safe to store in state."""
    id: int
    name: str
    is_active: bool = True
```

Convert in state: `self.items = [MyModel(**e.to_dict()) for e in entities]`

**Important**: Never store SQLAlchemy entity objects (those with relationships) directly in Reflex state — lazy-loaded relationships will fail outside the session context.

---

## 9. Roles & Authorization

Define new roles in `app/roles.py`:

```python
MY_FEATURE_ROLE = Role(name="my-feature", label="My Feature", group=MY_GROUP)
ALL_ROLES = [..., MY_FEATURE_ROLE]
```

Use in page factory: `admin_only=True` or `role=MY_FEATURE_ROLE.name`.

Use in navbar:

```python
requires_role(
    sidebar_item(label="My Feature", icon="star", url="/my-feature"),
    role=MY_FEATURE_ROLE.name,
)
```

---

## 10. Anti-Patterns

| Anti-pattern | Correct approach |
|---|---|
| Storing SQLAlchemy entity objects in state | Use `rx.Base` display models |
| Calling `service_registry()` at module level | Call inside functions/methods |
| Mutating state without `yield` in async gen | Always `yield` after mutations |
| Fat page functions | Decompose into `_section()` helpers |
| Logic in components | Move to state event handlers or `@rx.var` |
| `rx.asession()` in background tasks / callbacks | Use `get_asyncdb_session()` |
| `and` / `or` inside `rx.cond(...)` | Use `&` and `\|` operators |
| Calling a background task directly from a handler | `yield MyState.background_task` — always yield the method reference |
| Duplicating CRUD in repositories | Use `BaseRepository` methods directly; only add custom query methods |

---

## 11. File & Naming Conventions

```
state/my_feature_state.py        → MyFeatureState(rx.State)
components/my_feature_table.py   → my_feature_table() → rx.Component
components/my_feature_dialogs.py → create_dialog(), delete_dialog()
backend/models.py                → MyModel, MyModelDisplay
backend/repository.py            → MyModelRepository (static methods)
pages.py                         → create_my_feature_page(navbar)
configuration.py                 → MyFeatureConfig(BaseConfig)
```

---

## 12. Form Validation Pattern

Use a **dedicated `rx.State` subclass** (not mixed into the main feature state) to hold form field values, per-field error strings, and validation logic. This keeps form concerns isolated and testable.

**→ See [`examples/form_validation_example.py`](examples/form_validation_example.py) for the full annotated example.**

### Key rules

- Store each field as `str` — inputs are always strings; parse/validate explicitly.
- Store per-field error as `str` — empty string means no error.
- Decorate `validate_*` methods with `@rx.event` so the UI can bind them to `on_blur`.
- Expose `@rx.var` `is_form_valid` / `is_form_invalid` — bind to the submit button's `disabled` prop.
- `form_version: int` counter — increment in `initialize()` to force re-render of controlled inputs on reset.
- Async DB uniqueness checks (`validate_email_unique`) — attach to `on_blur`, **not** `on_change` (avoids a DB hit on every keystroke).
- Call `initialize()` from the parent state's `open_add_modal` / `open_edit_modal`, returning `[ValidationState.initialize(...)]`.
- Call `validate_all()` at the top of the submit handler to surface all errors before bailing out.

### Pattern summary

```python
class ItemValidationState(rx.State):
    form_version: int = 0       # increment on initialize() to reset controlled inputs
    name: str = ""              # one field var per input
    name_error: str = ""        # one error var per field (empty = no error)

    @rx.event
    def initialize(self, item: Item | None = None) -> None:
        # populate or reset all fields; clear all errors; form_version += 1
        ...

    def set_name(self, value: str) -> None:   # setter: update field + validate inline
        self.name = value
        self.validate_name()

    @rx.event
    def validate_name(self) -> None: ...      # sync validator → on_blur or on_change
    @rx.event
    async def validate_email_unique(self) -> None: ...  # async DB check → on_blur only
    @rx.event
    def validate_all(self) -> None: ...       # call before submit

    @rx.var
    def is_form_valid(self) -> bool: ...
    @rx.var
    def is_form_invalid(self) -> bool: return not self.is_form_valid

# Parent state opens modal and initialises the form in one call:
def open_add_modal(self) -> list[rx.event.EventSpec]:
    self.is_add_modal_open = True
    return [ItemValidationState.initialize()]

# Submit guard:
async def submit_item(self) -> AsyncGenerator:
    form_state = await self.get_state(ItemValidationState)
    if form_state.is_form_invalid:
        yield ItemValidationState.validate_all()
        return
    # use form_state.name, form_state.email, etc.
```

---

See the `examples/` folder alongside this SKILL.md:

| `state_example.py` | Full state class — loading, computed vars, pagination |

def _easter(year: int) -> date:
    """Gregorian Easter Sunday (anonymous Gregorian algorithm)."""
    a = year % 19
    b, c = divmod(year, 100)
    d, e = divmod(b, 4)
    f = (b + 8) // 25
    g = (b - f + 1) // 3
    h = (19 * a + b - d - g + 15) % 30
    i, k = divmod(c, 4)
    l = (32 + 2 * e + 2 * i - h - k) % 7  # noqa: E741
    m = (a + 11 * h + 22 * l) // 451
    month, day = divmod(h + l - 7 * m + 114, 31)
    return date(year, month, day + 1)

database schema must not write to it, so sign-in stops with a clear message
instead.
"""

from typing import Final

    """None when the database has the expected schema, else a message."""

def requires_admin[F: Callable[..., Any]](func: F) -> F:
    """Authorization decorator: allow the event only for authenticated admins.

    Enforces admin authorization server-side (over the websocket), independent

"""Database access of alloq users, granted from the desktop app.

The desktop app connects with the signed-in person's own Entra ID token. When
that person is a database admin (an Entra admin of the server, so a member of
`azure_pg_admin`), they can give other alloq users access: the user's Entra ID
principal is created if needed and gets the role `<database>_app` that the
migration `ee66ff77aa88` created. The user then logs in with their own token.
"""

import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable
from contextlib import AbstractAsyncContextManager, asynccontextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Final

from sqlalchemy import make_url, text
from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncConnection, AsyncSession, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

from appkit_commons.database.configuration import DatabaseConfig
from appkit_commons.database.session import get_asyncdb_session
from appkit_commons.registry import service_registry

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAINTENANCE_DATABASE: Final = "postgres"
"""Entra ID principals can only be created in this database."""

NOT_ADMIN = (
    "Dir fehlen die Admin-Rechte in der Datenbank. Nur eine Datenbank-"
    "Administratorin oder ein Datenbank-Administrator kann Zugriff vergeben."
)
NO_PRINCIPAL = (
    "Für {email} ließ sich kein Datenbank-Benutzer anlegen. Die E-Mail-Adresse "
    "muss der Microsoft-Anmeldung (UPN) entsprechen."
)

_ROLE = text("SELECT current_database() || '_app'")
_CAN_MANAGE = text(
    "SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = :role) "
    "THEN pg_has_role(current_user, :role, 'MEMBER WITH ADMIN OPTION') "
    "ELSE false END"
)
_MEMBERS = text(
    "SELECT m.rolname FROM pg_auth_members am "
    "JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = am.roleid "
    "JOIN pg_roles m ON m.oid = am.member "
    "WHERE r.rolname = :role"
)
_PRINCIPAL = text(
    "SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE lower(rolname) = lower(:name) "
    "ORDER BY rolname = :name DESC LIMIT 1"
)
_CREATE_PRINCIPAL = text("SELECT * FROM pgaadauth_create_principal(:name, false, false)")

type SessionFactory = Callable[[], AbstractAsyncContextManager[AsyncSession]]
type ConnectionFactory = Callable[[], AbstractAsyncContextManager[AsyncConnection]]


class DatabaseAccessError(Exception):
    """Granting or revoking failed; the message is shown to the user."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AccessOverview:
    can_manage: bool
    """The signed-in database login may grant and revoke the role."""
    members: frozenset[str]
    """Lower-cased names of the logins that hold the role directly."""


def quote_identifier(name: str) -> str:
    """A Postgres identifier in double quotes, safe for any role name."""
    if "\x00" in name:
        msg = "Role names cannot contain NUL"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return '"' + name.replace('"', '""') + '"'


@asynccontextmanager
async def maintenance_connection() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncConnection]:
    """A short connection to the `postgres` database with the same login.

    The desktop app's connect hook fills in user and token for every engine.
    """
    config = service_registry().get(DatabaseConfig)
    url = make_url(config.url).set(database=MAINTENANCE_DATABASE)
    engine = create_async_engine(url, poolclass=NullPool)
    try:
        async with engine.begin() as connection:
            yield connection
    finally:
        await engine.dispose()


async def _role(db: AsyncSession) -> str:
    return str((await db.execute(_ROLE)).scalar_one())


async def _can_manage(db: AsyncSession, role: str) -> bool:
    return bool((await db.execute(_CAN_MANAGE, {"role": role})).scalar_one())


async def _principal(db: AsyncSession, email: str) -> str | None:
    """The existing login of this email; an exact match wins over case."""
    result = await db.execute(_PRINCIPAL, {"name": email})
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()


class DatabaseAccess:
    """Grant and revoke the desktop role with the signed-in admin's rights."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        sessions: SessionFactory = get_asyncdb_session,
        maintenance: ConnectionFactory = maintenance_connection,
    ) -> None:
        self._sessions = sessions
        self._maintenance = maintenance

    async def overview(self) -> AccessOverview:
        async with self._sessions() as db:
            role = await _role(db)
            can_manage = await _can_manage(db, role)
            rows = (await db.execute(_MEMBERS, {"role": role})).scalars().all()
        return AccessOverview(
            can_manage=can_manage,
            members=frozenset(name.lower() for name in rows),
        )

    async def grant(self, email: str) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as db:
            role = await self._managed_role(db)
            principal = await _principal(db, email)
        if principal is None:
            principal = await self._create_principal(email)
        async with self._sessions() as db:
            await db.execute(
                text(f"GRANT {quote_identifier(role)} TO {quote_identifier(principal)}")
            )
        logger.info("Granted database access to a user")

    async def revoke(self, email: str) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as db:
            role = await self._managed_role(db)
            principal = await _principal(db, email)
            if principal is None:
                return
            await db.execute(
                text(
                    f"REVOKE {quote_identifier(role)} "
                    f"FROM {quote_identifier(principal)}"
                )
            )
        logger.info("Revoked database access of a user")

    async def _managed_role(self, db: AsyncSession) -> str:
        role = await _role(db)
        if not await _can_manage(db, role):
            raise DatabaseAccessError(NOT_ADMIN)
        return role

    async def _create_principal(self, email: str) -> str:
        """Create the Entra ID principal; only an Entra admin may do that."""
        try:
            async with self._maintenance() as connection:
                await connection.execute(_CREATE_PRINCIPAL, {"name": email})
        except DBAPIError as exc:
            logger.warning("Creating the Entra ID principal failed: %s", exc.orig)
            raise DatabaseAccessError(NO_PRINCIPAL.format(email=email)) from exc
        return email

"""Database access switch of one user row (desktop app only)."""

import reflex as rx

import appkit_mantine as mn
from appkit_user.authentication.backend.models import User

from app.desktop.db_access_state import DatabaseAccessState


def database_access_button(user: User) -> rx.Component:
    granted = DatabaseAccessState.members.contains(user.email.lower())
    return mn.tooltip(
        mn.action_icon(
            rx.icon("database", size=16),
            variant="subtle",
            color=rx.cond(granted, "green", "gray"),
            loading=DatabaseAccessState.pending_email == user.email,
            # data_disabled keeps the tooltip working on the disabled button
            data_disabled=~DatabaseAccessState.can_manage,
            aria_label="Datenbankzugriff",
            on_click=DatabaseAccessState.toggle(user.email),
        ),
        label=rx.cond(
            DatabaseAccessState.can_manage,
            rx.cond(granted, "Datenbankzugriff entziehen", "Datenbankzugriff geben"),
            rx.cond(
