"""Granting database access from the users page of the desktop app."""

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Callable
from contextlib import AbstractAsyncContextManager, asynccontextmanager
from typing import Any
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch

import pytest
from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
from sqlalchemy.sql.elements import TextClause

from app.desktop import db_access, db_access_state
from app.desktop.db_access import (
    NO_PRINCIPAL,
    NOT_ADMIN,
    AccessOverview,
    DatabaseAccess,
    DatabaseAccessError,
    maintenance_connection,
    quote_identifier,
)
from app.desktop.db_access_state import DatabaseAccessState

ROLE = "alloq_app"


class FakeResult:
    def __init__(self, value: Any) -> None:
        self._value = value

    def scalar_one(self) -> Any:
        return self._value

    def scalar_one_or_none(self) -> Any:
        return self._value

    def scalars(self) -> MagicMock:
        return MagicMock(all=lambda: self._value)


class FakeDatabase:
    """Answers the catalog queries of `db_access` and records every statement."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        can_manage: bool = True,
        members: list[str] | None = None,
        principals: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.can_manage = can_manage
        self.members = members or []
        self.principals = principals or {}
        self.statements: list[str] = []
        self.created: list[str] = []
        self.create_error: Exception | None = None

    async def execute(
        self, statement: TextClause, params: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> FakeResult:
        params = params or {}
        if statement is db_access._ROLE:
            return FakeResult(ROLE)
        if statement is db_access._CAN_MANAGE:
            return FakeResult(self.can_manage)
        if statement is db_access._MEMBERS:
            return FakeResult(self.members)
        if statement is db_access._PRINCIPAL:
            return FakeResult(self.principals.get(params["name"].lower()))
        if statement is db_access._CREATE_PRINCIPAL:
            if self.create_error:
                raise self.create_error
            self.created.append(params["name"])
            return FakeResult(None)
        self.statements.append(statement.text)
        return FakeResult(None)

    def factory(self) -> Callable[[], AbstractAsyncContextManager[Any]]:
        @asynccontextmanager
        async def _open() -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
            yield self

        return _open


def _access(db: FakeDatabase) -> DatabaseAccess:
    return DatabaseAccess(sessions=db.factory(), maintenance=db.factory())


class TestQuoteIdentifier:
    def test_quotes_and_escapes(self) -> None:
        assert quote_identifier("ada@x.de") == '"ada@x.de"'
        assert quote_identifier('a"; DROP ROLE x; --') == '"a""; DROP ROLE x; --"'

    def test_rejects_nul(self) -> None:
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="NUL"):
            quote_identifier("a\x00b")


class TestDatabaseAccess:
    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_overview_lowercases_members(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase(members=["Ada@X.de", "azure_pg_admin"])
        overview = await _access(db).overview()
        assert overview == AccessOverview(
            can_manage=True, members=frozenset({"ada@x.de", "azure_pg_admin"})
        )

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_grant_uses_the_existing_principal(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase(principals={"ada@x.de": "Ada@x.de"})
        await _access(db).grant("ada@x.de")
        assert db.created == []
        assert db.statements == ['GRANT "alloq_app" TO "Ada@x.de"']

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_grant_creates_a_missing_principal(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase()
        await _access(db).grant("bob@x.de")
        assert db.created == ["bob@x.de"]
        assert db.statements == ['GRANT "alloq_app" TO "bob@x.de"']

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_grant_needs_admin_rights(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase(can_manage=False)
        with pytest.raises(DatabaseAccessError, match="Admin-Rechte"):
            await _access(db).grant("bob@x.de")
        assert db.created == []
        assert db.statements == []

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_unknown_microsoft_account(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase()
        db.create_error = DBAPIError("SELECT", {}, Exception("no such principal"))
        with pytest.raises(DatabaseAccessError) as raised:
            await _access(db).grant("nobody@x.de")
        assert str(raised.value) == NO_PRINCIPAL.format(email="nobody@x.de")
        assert db.statements == []

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_revoke(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase(principals={"ada@x.de": "ada@x.de"})
        await _access(db).revoke("Ada@x.de")
        assert db.statements == ['REVOKE "alloq_app" FROM "ada@x.de"']

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_revoke_without_principal_does_nothing(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase()
        await _access(db).revoke("bob@x.de")
        assert db.statements == []

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_revoke_needs_admin_rights(self) -> None:
        db = FakeDatabase(can_manage=False, principals={"ada@x.de": "ada@x.de"})
        with pytest.raises(DatabaseAccessError, match="Admin-Rechte"):
            await _access(db).revoke("ada@x.de")
        assert db.statements == []


class TestMaintenanceConnection:
    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_connects_to_the_postgres_database(self) -> None:
        config = MagicMock(url="postgresql+psycopg://:@db.example:5432/alloq")
        connection = object()

        @asynccontextmanager
        async def _begin() -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
            yield connection

        engine = MagicMock(begin=_begin, dispose=AsyncMock())
        with (
            patch.object(db_access, "service_registry") as registry,
            patch.object(
                db_access, "create_async_engine", return_value=engine
            ) as create,
        ):
            registry.return_value.get.return_value = config
            async with maintenance_connection() as opened:
                assert opened is connection

        url = create.call_args.args[0]
        assert url.database == "postgres"
        assert url.host == "db.example"
        engine.dispose.assert_awaited_once()


def _login_state(*, is_admin: bool) -> MagicMock:
    user = MagicMock(is_admin=is_admin, user_id=1)

    async def _user() -> MagicMock:
        return user

    login_state = MagicMock()
    type(login_state).authenticated_user = property(lambda _self: _user())
    login_state.redir = AsyncMock(return_value=None)
    return login_state


def _state(*, is_admin: bool = True) -> DatabaseAccessState:
    state = DatabaseAccessState()
    object.__setattr__(
        state, "get_state", AsyncMock(return_value=_login_state(is_admin=is_admin))
    )
    return state


async def _run(handler: AsyncGenerator[Any]) -> list[Any]:
    return [event async for event in handler]


def _toasts(events: list[Any], kind: str) -> list[str]:
    return [str(e) for e in events if e is not None and kind in str(e)]


class TestDatabaseAccessState:
    @pytest.fixture
    def access(self) -> MagicMock:
        access = MagicMock()
        access.overview = AsyncMock(
            return_value=AccessOverview(
                can_manage=True, members=frozenset({"ada@x.de"})
            )
        )
        access.grant = AsyncMock()
        access.revoke = AsyncMock()
        with patch.object(db_access_state, "get_access", return_value=access):
            yield access

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_load_in_the_desktop_app(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        state = _state()
        with patch.object(db_access_state, "is_desktop", return_value=True):
            await _run(state.load())
        assert state.can_manage is True
        assert state.members == ["ada@x.de"]
        assert state.locked is False

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_load_on_the_server_does_nothing(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        state = _state()
        with patch.object(db_access_state, "is_desktop", return_value=False):
            await _run(state.load())
        access.overview.assert_not_called()
        assert state.locked is True

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_load_failure_locks_the_switch(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        access.overview.side_effect = RuntimeError("connection lost")
        state = _state()
        state.can_manage = True
        with patch.object(db_access_state, "is_desktop", return_value=True):
            await _run(state.load())
        assert state.can_manage is False
        assert state.members == []

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_load_needs_an_alloq_admin(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        state = _state(is_admin=False)
        with patch.object(db_access_state, "is_desktop", return_value=True):
            await _run(state.load())
        access.overview.assert_not_called()

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_toggle_grants(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        state = _state()
        state.can_manage = True
        events = await _run(state.toggle("bob@x.de"))
        access.grant.assert_awaited_once_with("bob@x.de")
        access.revoke.assert_not_called()
        assert _toasts(events, "success")
        assert state.pending_email == ""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_toggle_revokes_a_member(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        state = _state()
        state.can_manage = True
        state.members = ["ada@x.de"]
        await _run(state.toggle("Ada@x.de"))
        access.revoke.assert_awaited_once_with("Ada@x.de")
        access.grant.assert_not_called()

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_toggle_shows_the_access_error(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        access.grant.side_effect = DatabaseAccessError(NOT_ADMIN)
        state = _state()
        state.can_manage = True
        events = await _run(state.toggle("bob@x.de"))
        assert _toasts(events, "error")
        assert state.pending_email == ""

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_toggle_hides_unexpected_errors(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        access.grant.side_effect = RuntimeError("boom")
        state = _state()
        state.can_manage = True
        events = await _run(state.toggle("bob@x.de"))
        errors = _toasts(events, "error")
        assert errors
        assert "boom" not in errors[0]

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_toggle_without_db_admin_rights(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        state = _state()
        events = await _run(state.toggle("bob@x.de"))
        access.grant.assert_not_called()
        assert events == []

    @pytest.mark.asyncio
    async def test_toggle_needs_an_alloq_admin(self, access: MagicMock) -> None:
        state = _state(is_admin=False)
        state.can_manage = True
        await _run(state.toggle("bob@x.de"))

1. Microsoft-Entra-Authentifizierung aktivieren und die erste Person als
   Entra-Admin setzen (Typ „User“, ihr UPN). In knowledgeai-container ist das
   `pg_entra_admin`. Diese Person ist Datenbank-Admin und meldet sich wie alle
   anderen mit ihrem eigenen Konto an; `db_role` bleibt leer.
2. Die Migration `ee66ff77aa88` legt auf dem Server die Rolle
   `<datenbank>_app` an (`alloq_app`). Sie darf alle Tabellen lesen und ändern,
   auch die späterer Migrationen, aber das Schema nicht ändern. Die
   Datenbank-Admins (`azure_pg_admin`) dürfen sie weitergeben.
3. Zugriff vergeben: Die erste Person öffnet in der Desktop-App
   „Administration · Benutzer“ und klickt in der Zeile einer Person auf das
   Datenbank-Symbol. Die App legt den Entra-Prinzipal der Person an (falls es
   ihn noch nicht gibt) und gibt ihr die Rolle. Ein zweiter Klick entzieht die
   Rolle wieder. Grün heißt: hat Zugriff.
4. Netzwerk: Der Server muss von den Rechnern aus erreichbar sein (VPN oder
   Firewall-Regel). TLS ist Pflicht (`ssl_mode: require`).

Das Datenbank-Symbol gibt es nur in der Desktop-App, denn nur dort verbindet
sich die App mit dem Konto der angemeldeten Person. Ohne Admin-Rechte in der
Datenbank zeigt es den Zugriff nur an. Die E-Mail-Adresse in alloq muss dem
Microsoft-Anmeldenamen (UPN) entsprechen, auch in der Groß- und
Kleinschreibung, denn Postgres meldet die Person mit diesem Namen an.

216	## Entra ID login for PostgreSQL
217	
218	The alloq desktop app has no database password. Every person signs in with
219	Microsoft Entra ID, and the app sends their access token as the Postgres
220	password. This is off by default. It needs three things in Azure: the server
221	accepts Entra ID tokens, the app registration may ask for a token for Postgres,
222	and Postgres knows the principal and its rights.
223	
224	### Terraform
225	
226	Set `pg_entra_admin` and, for computers outside Azure, `pg_client_ip_ranges`:
227	
228	```hcl
229	pg_entra_admin = {
230	  object_id      = "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx" # Entra group of the database admins
231	  principal_name = "knai-db-admins"
232	  principal_type = "Group"                                # or User, ServicePrincipal
233	}
234	
235	pg_client_ip_ranges = {
236	  office = { start_ip_address = "203.0.113.10", end_ip_address = "203.0.113.10" }
237	}
238	```
239	
240	With `pg_entra_admin` set, Terraform:
241	
242	- turns on Entra ID login on the server. Password login stays on, because the
243	  apps and their migrations log in with the admin user from `<prefix>-db-*`,
244	- makes `pg_entra_admin` the Entra admin of the server,
245	- adds a firewall rule for every entry in `pg_client_ip_ranges`,
246	- adds to the app registration the public client redirect `http://localhost`
247	  and the delegated permission "Azure OSSRDBMS Database" `user_impersonation`,
248	  and grants admin consent for the whole tenant.
249	
250	With `create_app_registration = false`, Terraform does not manage the
251	registration. It adds the permission with `azuread_application_api_access`
252	and sets the public client redirects with `azuread_application_redirect_uris`.
253	That resource owns all public client redirects of the registration, so other
254	public client redirects of it are removed. Check in the portal that
255	"Allow public client flows" is on.
256	
257	Before the first apply, check two things:
258	
259	- The tenant has the service principal of "Azure OSSRDBMS Database"
260	  (`123cd850-d9df-40bd-94d5-c9f07b7fa203`). If the plan cannot find it, create it
261	  once with `az ad sp create --id 123cd850-d9df-40bd-94d5-c9f07b7fa203`.
262	- The account that runs Terraform may grant admin consent. If someone already
263	  granted consent in the portal, import that grant instead of creating a second
264	  one: `terraform import 'module.app_registration.azuread_service_principal_delegated_permission_grant.ossrdbms[0]' <grant id>`.
265	
266	### Postgres
267	
268	Postgres roles are not Azure resources, so Terraform does not create them. After
269	the apply, run once per principal:
270	
271	```bash
272	az login
273	scripts/postgres_entra_access.sh <keyvault_name> alloq knai-db-admins alloq-desktop
274	```
275	
276	The arguments are the Key Vault, the `keyvault_prefix` of the app, the Entra
277	admin, and the principal (an Entra group name or a user UPN). You must be the
278	Entra admin or a member of its group, and you need `psql` and read access to
279	the Key Vault. The script:
280	
281	1. logs in as the Entra admin with your token and creates the principal with
282	   `pgaadauth_create_principal`,
283	2. logs in as the server admin from `<prefix>-db-*`, which owns the app's
284	   tables, and grants the role `<database>_app` to the principal. The role may
285	   read and change all tables, also the ones of later migrations, but may not
286	   change the schema.
287	
288	Running the script again does no harm. With a group as principal, add people
289	to the Entra group; they log in as the group name. In the alloq desktop
290	configuration set `db_role` to the group name.

Desktop users connect to Postgres with their own Entra token. The pieces (2026-10-15):
- knowledgeai-container branch feature/alloq2: `pg_entra_admin` (the first alloq admin, a User) turns on Entra login; `pg_client_ip_ranges` adds firewall rules.
- alloq migration `ee66ff77aa88` creates `<db>_app` (alloq_app) as the table owner and grants it `TO azure_pg_admin WITH ADMIN OPTION`.
- alloq desktop users page: database icon per row (`app/desktop/db_access.py`, `db_access_state.py`). It creates the principal in the `postgres` db and grants the role with the signed-in admin's token. Desktop only.

**Why:** The user wants the first app user, a DB admin, to grant access, not a service principal. On Azure the Entra admin is not a superuser: it can run `pgaadauth_create_principal` (only in the `postgres` db) but can't grant on tables owned by the password admin. The ADMIN OPTION through azure_pg_admin closes that gap (tested on PG16).

**How to apply:** Each desktop user logs in as their own UPN (`db_role` empty), so the alloq email must match the UPN exactly. Prod uses `create_app_registration = false`. See also [[local-test-login]].

content.text:
The users page in the alloq desktop app now has a database button in each user row. An alloq admin who is also a database admin, normally the first user, can use it to grant or remove a person's database access. The full test suite passes (1057 tests, 86.9% coverage), but I haven't tried it against the real Azure server, and I didn't click through it in the running app.

**How it works**
- The button only appears in the desktop app, because only there does the app connect to the database with the signed-in person's own token. The web app connects with the shared server password and can't create Entra users.
- Granting creates the person's Entra login in the database if it doesn't exist yet, then gives them the role `alloq_app`. A second click takes the role away.
- Green means the person has access. If the signed-in person isn't a database admin, the button only shows the status and its tooltip says why.

**Why this needed a migration:** On Azure, the server's Entra admin is not a superuser. It can create Entra logins, but it can't grant rights on tables that belong to the password admin, which runs the migrations. So the new migration `ee66ff77aa88` creates `alloq_app` as the table owner and passes it to `azure_pg_admin` WITH ADMIN OPTION, so every database admin can grant it. I tested this in a local Postgres 16 container, including tables created by later migrations and the downgrade.

**Changes in alloq** (not committed, because your branch had other work in progress):
- the migration above, and the new revision added to [app/desktop/schema.py](app/desktop/schema.py)
- the grant logic in [app/desktop/db_access.py](app/desktop/db_access.py) and the page state in [app/desktop/db_access_state.py](app/desktop/db_access_state.py)
- the button in [app/components/db_access_button.py](app/components/db_access_button.py), wired up in [app/pages/users.py](app/pages/users.py)
- tests, and the setup steps in [doc/desktop.md](doc/desktop.md)

`task lint` still fails on 16 older `ICN001` findings in files I didn't touch; the new code is clean.

**Changes in knowledgeai-container:** commit `cd313ad` on `feature/alloq2` (not pushed). It removes the SQL script from my last change, since the migration and the users page now do its job. `pg_entra_admin` now defaults to a single user instead of a group, and the docs are updated.

**Two things to know:**
- **Use a user, not a group, as `pg_entra_admin`.** Every desktop user logs in with their own Microsoft sign-in name. With a group, members would have to log in with the group name, and that clashes with personal logins.
- **The email in alloq must exactly match the person's Microsoft sign-in name, including upper and lower case.** Postgres looks up the login by that exact name.

Sources:
- [Manage Microsoft Entra roles in Azure Database for PostgreSQL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/security/security-manage-entra-users)
- [Manage Microsoft Entra roles (Azure China docs)](https://docs.azure.cn/en-us/postgresql/security/security-manage-entra-users)
